value: acoustic startle response as the first response to AHD exposure in four of six tagged porpoises
eye: ear; whole-animal behavioural response (acoustic startle) of free-ranging tagged porpoises
method: tagged free-ranging exposure to an acoustic harassment device, received level measured on the animal, startle detected in tag movement data
conditions: Free-ranging harbour porpoises off Denmark: six animals incidentally trapped in pound nets (tagged May 2018, September 2019, October 2019), tagged within 24 h of discovery, handled on a boat for at most 19 min (mean 9 min), fitted with suction-cup DTAGs (sound, 3D movement, plus GPS in n = 3 or ECG in n = 2) and released; exposure began 16 to 202 min after release with the animals free-swimming at sea. Stimulus: a commercial Loftech acoustic harassment device (source level 189 dB re 1 µPa rms at 1 m) for 15 min. Received level measured on the animal's tag: initial RL 98 to 132 dB re 1 µPa (rms-fast, 125 ms) at initial ranges of 0.9 to 7 km (band-passed 10-46 kHz). Control: the 15 min immediately before each exposure as baseline; the authors also ran 80-dB-reduced control playbacks to a separate untagged animal. The authors note that capture, handling and tagging may have influenced responses. In the six-animal sample, startle occurred in four animals (HP1-HP3, HP6); two did not startle.
